oneLine: Runs the final leg: delivery waves at a station, packages taken in when loads arrive, partner routes, delivery attempts, retries and returns.

rows.title: Keep the list of delivery stations
rows.story: Node-topology announces every node. Only delivery stations matter here; a wave or a partner can be set up only for a station that is on this list.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, keep it only if it is a delivery station

rows.title: Keep the stop of each labelled package
rows.story: When a label is issued, the package's stop key and order assignment are kept. Packages for one address share a stop, so they take one place in a wave.
rows.policy: Whenever a label is issued, keep the package's stop key; a label without a usable key is ignored

rows.title: Schedule a delivery wave
rows.story: A station planner opens a wave: an induction cut-off, a delivery window and how many stops it can take. Packages already waiting at the station are taken into it, oldest first.

then.does: adds the wave to its copy so promises can use it
adds the wave to the network copy its search uses

rows.title: Take in packages when a load arrives
rows.story: When a load reaches a delivery station, each package goes into the earliest wave that still accepts it. A package no wave accepts waits at the station and a deferral is announced.
rows.policy: Whenever a load reaches a delivery station, put each package on the earliest open wave or defer it

then.does: updates the room left on the wave; a deferred package flags its promise as at risk
updates the room left on the wave in its network copy

rows.title: Declare what a stop costs
rows.story: A station planner declares the cost of one stop on a wave that is still running. Order-sourcing adds it to the cost of the routes it compares.

then.does: uses it as the wave's per-stop cost when comparing routes

rows.title: Close induction on a wave
rows.story: A station planner stops taking packages into a wave, so routes can be planned on a fixed set of packages.

rows.title: Cancel a wave
rows.story: A station planner cancels a wave that is still open. Its packages move to the next eligible wave in the same step, or wait at the station.

then.does: flags promises whose route used the wave as at risk
marks the wave as cancelled in its network copy

rows.title: Contract a delivery partner
rows.story: A station planner signs up a delivery service partner for a station, with the van capacity of its routes.

rows.title: Deactivate a delivery partner
rows.story: A station planner deactivates a partner. It gets no new routes; routes already planned are not re-checked.

rows.title: Plan a partner's route in a wave
rows.story: A station planner gives a partner a numbered list of stops from a wave whose induction is closed. The route must fit the van, use only packages of the wave and keep one address in one stop.

rows.title: Dispatch a wave
rows.story: A station planner sends the wave out. Packages that no route holds are moved to the next wave, and a wave with no route completes at once.

rows.title: Start a route
rows.story: An operator starts a planned route of a dispatched wave. Every package goes out for delivery, and each stop gets an arrival window of up to two hours inside the wave's delivery window.

then.does: records an out-for-delivery scan and keeps the arrival window of each package

rows.title: Record a delivery attempt
rows.story: The driver records for each package whether it was delivered or failed. A package is delivered at most once, and the route completes when every package has an attempt.

then.does: records a delivered or failed-delivery scan for the package

rows.title: Retry a failed delivery, or send it back
rows.story: After a failed attempt the package goes on the next eligible wave. After the third failure it is not retried: a return to sender starts.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt fails, place the package on the next wave unless it was the third failure

then.does: marks the package as returned to sender

rows.title: Flag a drop-off point that keeps failing
rows.story: Each attempt updates the profile of its stop. After two failed visits for not-home or access problems within 60 days, the point is flagged for the packages affected. A flag changes no route.
rows.policy: Whenever an attempt is recorded, update the stop's profile; two failed visits flag the point

then.does: keeps the flag on every package of the stop

hotspots.text: A route stays out for delivery until every package has an attempt. If the driver skips one, the route and its wave stay open.
Deactivating a partner re-checks nothing: routes already planned keep the partner and the van capacity read at planning time.
Failure reasons are free text and the optional outcome detail is dormant until a client sends it, so delivery-point flags depend on clients adopting it.
The arrival window is spread evenly across the wave's window: there is no travel-time or position data to refine it.
Service-area assignments are kept but no decision reads them yet.

opportunities.text: Entrance, parking and locker knowledge for a drop-off point is left to a later item that needs its own model change.
